company.name: Center for a New American Security

profile_text.body:
The Center for a New American Security is a nonprofit organization founded in 2007 and headquartered in Washington, DC. Its website describes it as developing strong, pragmatic and principled national security and defense policies. Much of the material it publishes concerns artificial intelligence and its implications for national security.

The site's AI commentary covers several threads. It notes that artificial intelligence systems continue to progress at a steady pace, a trend it says has fed forecasts about artificial general intelligence. It also carries analysis arguing that an upcoming Trump-Xi summit is likely to disappoint the leaders of top AI labs that have recently called for urgent, coordinated pacing of frontier AI progress, and it states that the path forward is to lengthen the United States' AI lead by expanding, not weakening, technology protections, starting with closing three priority gaps, the first being remote access. The site also quotes Janet Egan, described there as an AI policy expert and adjunct senior fellow at the Centre for a New American Security, saying that certain incidents were "emblematic of a general trend in AI" in which capabilities outpace other considerations.

The facts held about the organization record no lawsuits and no MCP servers. Its profile lists it as a nonprofit based in Washington, DC, with Washington as its associated legal jurisdiction.
